parameters.description:
Labels and annotations: the request holds the whole set of ai-grid/* keys
and the location label, so one on the hub but left out is removed. Other
keys may be sent back as read; adding or changing one is InvalidArgument,
and so is an ai-grid/latitude or ai-grid/longitude annotation that isn't
a plain decimal number (no exponent, no comma, no N/S/E/W) within
-90..90 or -180..180, the values status.location reads.

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description:
Lock requires object.metadata.version: without one the request is
InvalidArgument. A non-zero version is checked against the hub's
resourceVersion with or without lock, before the labels, so a stale one
is Aborted whatever the request changes, even nothing.

post.summary:
Creates (= deploys) a model: commits its LLMInferenceService to the
placed clusters' indexes, and its ExternalModel and MaaSModelRef to the
ingress index, in the Git catalog.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: id / metadata.name and spec.model.uri are required. status is ignored.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Model id (equals metadata.name).

parameters.name: resource_version
parameters.description:
Expected version: when set (non-zero), delete fails with Aborted unless
it equals the stored metadata.version. Zero skips the check.

parameters.name: object.id
parameters.description: Unique identifier. Equals metadata.name (DNS-1123 label).

schema.description:
Model is a deployable LLM inference workload on the AI Grid.

It is committed to the backend's Git catalog: an LLMInferenceService
(serving.kserve.io/v1alpha2) that Argo CD delivers to the clusters the
placement names, and an ExternalModel and MaaSModelRef that publish it
through the grid on the ingress clusters.

The `spec` contains the desired details and may be modified by the user.
The `status` contains the current status and is provided by the system.

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description: When true, update fails with Aborted unless metadata.version matches.

get.summary:
Deprecated: use ListPlacementClusters, which answers the same list as
`clusters`. Despite its name, this RPC answers cluster names, not values
of the cluster's `location` label (those are in a model's
status.placement.locations). It is removed once its clients have moved
(docs/API_CONTRACT.md, "Expand, migrate, contract").

Clusters a model can be placed on: unique sorted names of the
ManagedClusters labelled ai-grid/enabled "true" and ai-grid/role
inference or combined that are Available and Compliant with the ready
Policy (AI_GRID_READY_POLICY). These are the values a placement's
`name In [...]` takes.

schema.description:
Subscription is a MaaS entitlement that binds identity subjects to models
with token rate limits and a priority.

It maps to the spoke-cluster Kubernetes CR MaaSSubscription
(apiVersion: maas.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1). It is not an OLM Subscription,
not an AAP license subscription, and not OSAC SERVICE_TIER_MAAS
("Metal as a Service").

The `spec` contains the desired details and may be modified by the user.
The `status` contains the current status and is provided by the system.

Maximum number of results to be returned by the server. When not specified all

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the tenant (Keycloak organization id / UUID).

metadata.description:
metadata.name is the organization name. metadata.version is kept in the
organization attribute ai-grid/resource-version: 1 on Create, bumped on
every Update this backend makes, and 1 for an organization without the
attribute (created in Keycloak directly). metadata.creation_timestamp comes from
the attribute ai-grid/create-time (RFC 3339), stamped on Create; it's
unset for an organization created elsewhere. Both are output only.

schema.description:
A tenant groups resources and users.
Backed by a Keycloak Organization in the shared platform realm (KEYCLOAK_REALM),
not by a Keycloak realm per tenant.

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description:
object.metadata.version is required, with or without lock: without one
the request is InvalidArgument. It's checked against the stored version
(Keycloak organization attribute ai-grid/resource-version), so a stale
one is Aborted. Every organization reads as version 1 or more. Every update that writes bumps
the version; one whose update_mask names only id, metadata.version or
metadata.creation_timestamp writes nothing and returns the tenant as
stored. The backend serializes its own writes per tenant, so of two
updates at the same version the second is Aborted. An edit made in
Keycloak directly isn't versioned.

id.description: Resource name (equals metadata.name on the CR).

v1AuthPolicy.description: AuthPolicy is a MaaSAuthPolicy: groups/users allowed to call a set of models.

v1AuthPolicyModelRef.description: AuthPolicyModelRef references a MaaSModelRef granted by an AuthPolicy.

total.description:
GPU devices on the cluster's GPU nodes, as GPU Feature Discovery counts
them: the sum of each node's `count`. That is physical GPUs, except on a
node with MIG strategy "single", where GFD's count is the MIG devices
(GFD replaces the physical count there and reports none; under "mixed"
it stays the physical count).

node_count.description: Nodes with at least one GPU.

configurations.description:
The distinct node configurations (vendor, product, memory, GPUs per node,
sharing), each with how many nodes have it, most nodes first, then by
product. One entry is the usual case, for example NVIDIA-L4 with 1 GPU per
node on 2 nodes.

total.description: Total number of items that match the search criteria.

type.description: Condition type as defined by the owning controller.

status.description: Whether the object is in the condition.

last_transition_time.description: Last time the condition changed from one status to another.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason in CamelCase, when the controller provides one.

observed_generation.description: Generation of the object the condition was computed for; zero when unknown.

v1Condition.description: One entry of a Kubernetes-style status.conditions list.

v1ConditionStatus.description:
Status of a condition. Kubernetes `Unknown` is reported as UNSPECIFIED.

 - CONDITION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: The system cannot decide whether the object is in the condition.
 - CONDITION_STATUS_TRUE: The object is in the condition.
 - CONDITION_STATUS_FALSE: The object is not in the condition.

product.description:
`nvidia.com/gpu.product` as GPU Feature Discovery writes it, for example
"NVIDIA-L4" or "NVIDIA-H200"; MIG and time-slicing suffixes kept.

memory_mib.description:
`nvidia.com/gpu.memory`, MiB per GPU (per MIG device under MIG
strategy "single").

gpus_per_node.description:
`nvidia.com/gpu.count`: physical GPUs, or MIG devices under MIG
strategy "single" (see ClusterGPUs.total).

sharing.description: How these nodes share or slice their GPUs.

v1GPUConfiguration.description: Nodes that share one GPU configuration.

count.description:
`nvidia.com/gpu.count`: physical GPUs, or MIG devices under MIG
strategy "single" (see ClusterGPUs.total).

sharing.description: How the node shares or slices its GPUs.

ready.description: The node's Ready condition is True.

replicas.description: `nvidia.com/gpu.replicas`: schedulable units per GPU; 1 without sharing.

v1GPUSharing.description: How a node's GPUs are shared or sliced.

ref_name.description: Name of the AIGuardrail in the tenant namespace.

checks.description: Selected check names; empty means all checks in the policy.

v1GuardrailAttachment.description: GuardrailAttachment attaches an AIGuardrail policy by name.

id.description: Unique identifier of the managed cluster. For hub CRs this equals metadata.name.

v1ManagedCluster.description:
Hub-side ACM/OCM ManagedCluster inventory object.

The `spec` contains the desired details and may be modified by the user.
The `status` contains the current status and is provided by the system.

last_transition_time.description: Unset when the hub recorded none.

site_name.description:
`ai-grid/site-name`, surrounding whitespace removed. Kept whether or not
there are coordinates.

latitude.description:
Decimal degrees, -90..90. Unset when there are no coordinates; 0 is a
valid latitude.

longitude.description:
Decimal degrees, -180..180. Unset when there are no coordinates; 0 is a
valid longitude.

problem.description:
What is wrong with the coordinate annotations, for a hub admin to fix,
for example `ai-grid/latitude "40,7" is not a decimal number of
degrees, such as 40.7128 or -74.006`. Several problems are joined with
"; ". Empty when there is nothing to fix; missing annotations are not a
problem. Meant to be shown as is; match on it in no code.

region.description:
The cloud region the cluster runs in, from its
`region.open-cluster-management.io` claim (for example "us-east-2"), as
a fact whatever `source` is. Empty when the agent reports none, as on
most on-premises clusters.

v1ManagedClusterLocation.description:
Where a cluster is. A hub admin sets it once with the ManagedCluster
annotations `ai-grid/latitude`, `ai-grid/longitude` (decimal degrees) and
`ai-grid/site-name`; see the README, "Cluster locations".

`latitude` and `longitude` are both set or both unset. Without either
annotation, a cluster in a known cloud region gets approximate
coordinates (source CLOUD_REGION). When the annotations are wrong, the
coordinates are unset, `source` is NONE and `problem` says what to fix:
the backend never falls back to the region past a mistake.

v1ManagedClusterLocationSource.description:
Where a cluster's coordinates come from.

 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_LOCATION_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED: Not reported; a client also reads a source added after it was built as
UNSPECIFIED.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_LOCATION_SOURCE_NONE: No coordinates: no annotations and no known cloud region, or
annotations with a `problem`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_LOCATION_SOURCE_ANNOTATIONS: The `ai-grid/latitude` and `ai-grid/longitude` annotations, as the hub
admin set them.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_LOCATION_SOURCE_CLOUD_REGION: Approximate: the city or area the cloud provider names for `region`,
used when neither annotation is set. Good for a pin on a world map, not
for the data center's position; a UI should say it is approximate.

hub_accepts_client.description: Whether the hub accepts the spoke cluster client.

v1ManagedClusterSpec.description: Desired state of a hub ManagedCluster.

v1ManagedClusterState.description:
metadata.deletion_timestamp set                    -> DETACHING
  no conditions at all                               -> UNSPECIFIED
  HubAcceptedManagedCluster not True                 -> NOT_ACCEPTED
  ManagedClusterJoined not True, and
    ManagedClusterImportSucceeded False with reason
      ManagedClusterImporting                        -> IMPORTING
      ManagedClusterImportFailed                     -> IMPORT_FAILED
    otherwise                                        -> PENDING_IMPORT
  ManagedClusterConditionAvailable True              -> READY
  ManagedClusterConditionAvailable False             -> OFFLINE
  otherwise (Unknown or absent)                      -> UNKNOWN

"Not True" means False or absent. The ACM console's "needs approval" (a
pending CSR) and its hosted-cluster states aren't derived: the backend
reads neither CSRs nor HostedClusters, so such a cluster is PENDING_IMPORT.

 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_UNSPECIFIED: The hub has reported no condition yet; a client also reads a state added
after it was built as UNSPECIFIED.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_READY: Joined and available. ACM console: `ready`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_OFFLINE: Joined; the agent reports the cluster unavailable (Available False, for
example the kube-apiserver is down). ACM console: `offline`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_UNKNOWN: Joined; the hub has no current report (Available Unknown or absent,
usually an expired lease). ACM console: `unknown`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_PENDING_IMPORT: Accepted, not joined, import not started or not reported. ACM console:
`pendingimport`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_IMPORTING: Accepted, not joined, the import controller is applying the klusterlet.
ACM console: `importing`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_IMPORT_FAILED: Accepted, not joined, the import failed. ACM console: `importfailed`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_NOT_ACCEPTED: The hub hasn't accepted the cluster (HubAcceptedManagedCluster absent or
False, for example after hub_accepts_client was set to false). ACM
console: `notaccepted`.
 - MANAGED_CLUSTER_STATE_DETACHING: The ManagedCluster is being deleted and its agent removed. ACM console:
`detaching`.
v1ManagedClusterState.title:
Lifecycle state of a ManagedCluster, one per state the ACM console shows.
Checked in this order, the first that applies wins:

available.description: True when the ManagedCluster Available condition is True.

joined.description: True when the ManagedCluster Joined condition is True.

available_condition.description:
Raw Available condition status ("True", "False", "Unknown", …). Empty when absent.
The backend derives `state` from it and the other conditions; read
`state` for Ready, Offline or Unknown.

provisioning.description:
AI Grid provisioning, from the cluster's compliance with the hub's
ai-grid-ready Policy (by default ai-grid-policies/ai-grid-ready):
"Compliant" (provisioned), "NonCompliant", or "Pending" (placed, no
result yet). Empty when the Policy doesn't cover the cluster, for
example because it isn't labelled ai-grid/enabled=true, or when the
Policy can't be read.

conditions.description: `status.conditions`, as the hub reports them, in the hub's order.

kubernetes_version.description:
`status.version.kubernetes`, for example "v1.34.9". Empty until the
cluster's agent reports it.

capacity.description:
`status.capacity`: what the cluster's nodes provide, as Kubernetes
quantity strings keyed by resource name (for example "cpu": "68",
"memory": "273509824Ki", "nvidia.com/gpu": "1"). Empty until the agent
reports it.

cluster_claims.description:
`status.clusterClaims`, as the cluster's agent reports them, for example
`consoleurl.cluster.open-cluster-management.io`,
`platform.open-cluster-management.io` and
`product.open-cluster-management.io`.

gpus.description:
The cluster's GPUs, from ACM Search's index of its nodes and the labels
NVIDIA GPU Feature Discovery puts on them. Unset when Search isn't
available or hasn't indexed the cluster; `capacity["nvidia.com/gpu"]`
still counts its schedulable GPUs then.

ai_grid_member.description:
True when the cluster is an AI Grid member: its `ai-grid/enabled` label
is exactly "true", the label selector the hub's AI Grid Placements
match. A cluster joins or leaves the grid through Update, by setting or
removing that label in `metadata.labels`.

state.description:
The cluster's lifecycle state, derived from its conditions and its
deletion timestamp in the order the ACM console uses. UNSPECIFIED until
the hub reports any condition.

state_message.description:
The message of the condition that decided `state`, for example "Managed
cluster is available" or "Try to import managed cluster, error: ...".
Empty when that condition has no message or is absent.

location.description: Where the cluster is, for a map. Always set.

v1ManagedClusterStatus.description: Observed state of a hub ManagedCluster.

creation_timestamp.description: Time of creation of the object.

deletion_timestamp.description: Time of deletion of the object.

creator.description: Creator contains the identifier of the user or group that created the object.

tenant.description: Tenant contains the identifier of the tenant that the object belongs to.

name.description: Mandatory, immutable, and unique within scope. Must be a valid RFC 1123 DNS label.

labels.description: Labels contains key-value pairs for organizing and selecting objects.

annotations.description: Annotations contains arbitrary metadata for objects.

version.description: Version is a numeric field that is automatically incremented with every change to the object.

v1Metadata.description: Metadata common to all kinds of objects.

v1Model.description:
Model is a deployable LLM inference workload on the AI Grid.

It is committed to the backend's Git catalog: an LLMInferenceService
(serving.kserve.io/v1alpha2) that Argo CD delivers to the clusters the
placement names, and an ExternalModel and MaaSModelRef that publish it
through the grid on the ingress clusters.

The `spec` contains the desired details and may be modified by the user.
The `status` contains the current status and is provided by the system.

phase.description:
READY when every report from the cluster says ready; PENDING when one
says not ready (or not found) or one is missing. Git mode never sets
FAILED; PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE is only a whole model's phase.

reason.description:
Ready, NotReady (a report says not ready or not found) or NoReport (the
cluster hasn't reported the object yet).

message.description:
What the cluster reported, for example "LLMInferenceService not ready"
or "LLMInferenceService ready; no MaaSModelRef report".

v1ModelClusterStatus.description:
The model on one placed cluster. In git mode it comes from the hub's
status Policies: the cluster's models-ready report of the model's
LLMInferenceService (Ready=True), and, on a combined cluster, which is
also an ingress cluster, its model-refs-ready report of the model's
MaaSModelRef (phase Ready). Output only.

image.description:
Runtime image. Required when spec.base_refs is empty. With base_refs it
may be empty, and the presets' image applies: KServe merges the
LLMInferenceServiceConfigs named in baseRefs under the service's own
spec, and an empty image in the service doesn't override theirs
(combineBaseRefsConfig and mergeSpecs in
pkg/controller/v1alpha2/llmisvc/config_merge.go,
red-hat-data-services/kserve rhoai-3.6 at 40fa1a1). The backend can't
see the presets on the clusters, so it can't check that one sets an
image: if none does, Kubernetes refuses the workload on the cluster
("image: Required value"), the model never becomes ready there, and its
status says so. A blank image, or one with a space or tab, is
InvalidArgument.

requests.description:
Resource requests (cpu, memory, nvidia.com/gpu, ...): Kubernetes
quantities, which must parse and be non-negative. The values the
container can't have are InvalidArgument, as Kubernetes would refuse
them on every cluster: an extended resource such as nvidia.com/gpu that
isn't a whole number, a request above its limit, and, for the resources
Kubernetes can't overcommit (extended resources and hugepages-*), a
request that differs from its limit. Such a resource with a request and
no limit is saved with the request as its limit, as Kubernetes requires
the limit (validateResourceRequirements in kubernetes/kubernetes
pkg/apis/core/validation). An Update that replaces requests and not
limits drops each such limit that equalled its saved request, so the
limit follows the new request, and a removed request takes its limit
with it. A rule across the two maps is checked by the server only.

limits.description: Resource limits: Kubernetes quantities, as requests.

v1ModelPhase.description:
Derived model phase.

In git mode, while no cluster has reported the model, the phase is
UNSPECIFIED with reason SavedToGit. Once one has, the phase is, in this
order of precedence:

  - READY (reason Ready): every ingress cluster reports the model's
    MaaSModelRef ready, and every placed cluster is READY in `clusters`.
  - PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE (reason PartiallyAvailable): every ingress cluster
    reports the MaaSModelRef ready, at least one placed cluster is READY
    and at least one is not.
  - PENDING (reason NotReady): otherwise, including while an ingress
    cluster reports the MaaSModelRef not ready or hasn't reported it.

The ingress clusters are those the catalog status Policy lists and those
labelled ai-grid/enabled "true" and ai-grid/role ingress or combined; each
must report. READY and PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE need at least one: with none,
nothing shows the model published, so it is PENDING, and the message ends
"no ingress cluster has reported the MaaSModelRef".

Git mode never reports FAILED: the status Policies can't tell a model
that failed from one that is still starting. The order is the one the
console's Models page uses (READY, PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE, FAILED, then the
PENDING cases; proposal P13).

 - MODEL_PHASE_PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE: Serving on some of the clusters its placement names but not all (see
above). Only a whole model has it; a cluster in ModelStatus.clusters is
READY or PENDING.

cluster_sets.description: Cluster sets to draw from. Empty means every bound set.

number_of_clusters.description: Cap on selected clusters. Unset means all matching.

v1ModelPlacement.description: ACM Placement desired state (subset used by the Models API).

selected_clusters.description:
Selected cluster names (ManagedCluster names): the values of the
placement's `name In [...]`, as ListPlacementClusters answers them.

locations.description:
Unique sorted values of the `location` label of the selected clusters
(P8): where they are, not which clusters they are. Several clusters can
share one location, so these are not cluster names and a placement can't
name them; use selected_clusters for that. A selected cluster without a
location label adds nothing. Output only.

phase.description: Pending, Ready, Unhealthy, Failed, or Invalid.

v1ModelRegistration.description: ModelRegistration is a MaaSModelRef's catalog status for a referenced model.

max_concurrency.description: Progressive only: clusters at once (integer or percent like "20%").

works.description:
Per-cluster work summaries when available. Never set in git mode; see
ModelStatus.clusters.

gateway_refs.description:
Gateway refs. Empty uses the product default
(openshift-ingress/openshift-ai-inference).

managed_route.description: When true, controller manages the HTTPRoute (spec.router.route: {}).

scheduler.description:
When true, inference scheduler is created (spec.router.scheduler), with
its metrics served over HTTPS so the grid operator can scrape them.

max_replicas.description: Maximum replicas (required when scaling is set).

keda.description: Whether KEDA scaling is enabled. Must be true when scaling is set.

triggers.description: KEDA scale triggers (at least one required when keda is true).

uri.description: Artifact URI (hf://, oci://, s3://, pvc://, http(s)://).

name.description:
Deprecated: a model is served as its id, the name tenants send in the
request model field. Output: always the name the model is served as,
which is the id, or for a model saved before that change, the name it
still serves until its next update switches it to the id. Input: must be
empty or the id (or, on update, the name a read returned); any other value
is InvalidArgument. For a human-readable name, use annotation
openshift.io/display-name.

model.description: Where the artifact comes from and the name clients send.

replicas.description: Static replica count. Mutually exclusive with scaling.

base_refs.description:
LLMInferenceServiceConfig preset names merged under the spec. Each is a
name with no whitespace; an empty or blank name is InvalidArgument.

main.description:
Main container of the workload template. Its image may be empty only
when base_refs names a preset (see ModelContainer.image).

placement.description:
Where to deploy. Required: names at least one cluster by the ACM `name`
label (`name In [...]` or a `name` match label); the model is listed in
each named cluster's index in the Git catalog. A cluster that a create or
update adds must be a ManagedCluster on the hub, or the call is
InvalidArgument naming it, with a google.rpc.ResourceInfo detail per
unknown cluster (resource_type
`type.googleapis.com/ai_grid.v1.ManagedCluster`, resource_name the
cluster); Models/ListPlacementClusters lists the clusters a model can run
on.

rollout.description:
Rollout. Only strategy All (the default) is accepted: Argo CD delivers to
every placed cluster at once.

v1ModelSpec.description: Desired state of a Model (trimmed LLMInferenceService.spec + ACM placement).

reason.description:
Reason of the condition that decided phase. In git mode: SavedToGit
while no cluster has reported, else Ready, PartiallyAvailable or
NotReady with the phase.

message.description:
Message of the condition that decided phase. In git mode, while a
cluster has reported: where the model is ready, for example "Not ready
on site-a; ready on site-b; no report from site-c".

placement.description: Placement status when placement is set.

rollout.description:
ManifestWorkReplicaSet status when placement is set. Git mode has no
ManifestWorkReplicaSet and never sets it; each placed cluster's status
is in `clusters`.

clusters.description:
The model on each cluster its placement names (the clusters in
placement.selected_clusters), one entry per cluster in cluster-name
order, from what the hub's status Policies report. Empty while no
cluster has reported (reason SavedToGit). Ingress clusters the model
isn't placed on, which publish it but don't run it, have no entry; their
reports count in `phase` and `message`. Output only.

locations.description:
Despite the name, cluster names, not `location` labels: the same list as
ModelsListPlacementClustersResponse.clusters.

v1ModelsListLocationsResponse.description:
Response of ListLocations (P7). ListLocations is deprecated: use
ListPlacementClusters.

clusters.description:
Unique sorted ManagedCluster names (metadata.name, which ACM also sets as
the cluster's `name` label): the values a placement's `name In [...]`
takes.

v1ResourceRefStatus.description: ResourceRefStatus is the state of one object a MaaS resource references or generates.

id.description: Unique identifier of the subscription. Equals metadata.name.

v1Subscription.description:
Subscription is a MaaS entitlement that binds identity subjects to models
with token rate limits and a priority.

It maps to the spoke-cluster Kubernetes CR MaaSSubscription
(apiVersion: maas.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1). It is not an OLM Subscription,
not an AAP license subscription, and not OSAC SERVICE_TIER_MAAS
("Metal as a Service").

The `spec` contains the desired details and may be modified by the user.
The `status` contains the current status and is provided by the system.

namespace.description:
Model namespace. Empty means the platform default model namespace: the
subscription's own namespace, where the Models API publishes each
model's MaaSModelRef (not the namespace its LLMInferenceService runs in).
The backend writes it filled in, so reads return it.

token_rate_limits.description:
Token rate limits for this model. Required unless unlimited is true.
Must be empty when unlimited is true.

unlimited.description: Access without a token budget. Mutually exclusive with token_rate_limits.

guardrails.description: Guardrails for this model within the subscription.

display_name.description:
Output enrichment from MaaSModelRef annotations. Ignored on write.
The openshift.io/display-name annotation of the MaaSModelRef this ref
names, which the Models API copies from the Model's own annotation. Set
only with model_id; empty when the model has no display name.

description.description:
Output enrichment from MaaSModelRef annotations. Ignored on write.
The openshift.io/description annotation of the same MaaSModelRef, as
display_name.

model_id.description:
Output only; ignored on write. The id of the Model (ai_grid.v1.Models)
this ref names: set when name and namespace are those of the MaaSModelRef
the Models API publishes for that model, the one in its catalog entry.
Empty when the ref names a MaaSModelRef the Models API didn't write: in
another namespace, or for a model the catalog doesn't have. A client
joins a ref to its model by model_id == Model.id, with no namespace of
its own; on write it sends the model's id as name and leaves namespace
empty.

v1SubscriptionModelRef.description: SubscriptionModelRef references a model and optional token rate limits.

v1SubscriptionOrganization.description: SubscriptionOrganization identifies the organization that administers a subscription.

v1SubscriptionOwner.description: SubscriptionOwner names the groups and users that own the entitlement.

owner.description: Identity subjects entitled by this subscription.

model_refs.description: Models this subscription applies to, with optional per-model rate limits.

priority.description: Relative priority among subscriptions (higher wins when policies conflict).

organization.description:
The organization that administers the subscription. Required: Create
and Update answer InvalidArgument without it. Immutable once set.

token_metadata.description: Metadata for token attribution and metering.

inference_priority.description:
Scheduling priority for inference under this subscription. Distinct from
priority. When unset, no InferenceObjective is created.

guardrails.description: Guardrail policies attached to every model accessed through this subscription.

v1SubscriptionSpec.description: Desired state of a MaaS Subscription.

phase.description: Controller-reported phase (for example "Active"). Empty until reconciled.

v1SubscriptionStatus.description: Observed state of a MaaS Subscription.

auth_policy.description: Managed MaaSAuthPolicy created with the subscription (<id>-policy).

auth_policies.description:
AuthPolicies in the subscription namespace whose modelRefs intersect the
subscription's models (includes the managed <id>-policy when present).

model_registrations.description: MaaSModelRef status for each referenced model that exists.

total.description: Total number of items that match the search criteria.

id.description: Unique identifier of the tenant (Keycloak organization id / UUID).

metadata.description:
metadata.name is the organization name. metadata.version is kept in the
organization attribute ai-grid/resource-version: 1 on Create, bumped on
every Update this backend makes, and 1 for an organization without the
attribute (created in Keycloak directly). metadata.creation_timestamp comes from
the attribute ai-grid/create-time (RFC 3339), stamped on Create; it's
unset for an organization created elsewhere. Both are output only.

v1Tenant.description:
A tenant groups resources and users.
Backed by a Keycloak Organization in the shared platform realm (KEYCLOAK_REALM),
not by a Keycloak realm per tenant.

email.description: Email address when present on the user.

enabled.description: Whether the Keycloak user is enabled.

v1TenantMember.description:
TenantMember is a Keycloak user that belongs to the tenant's Organization.
This is a read projection for listing; full user management is out of scope.

domains.description: Email domains associated with this tenant (DNS hostnames, lowercase).

total.description: Total number of members that match (before limit).
Total number of items that match the search criteria.

organization_id.description: Legacy organization id for metering when organization.id is unset.

v1TokenMetadata.description: TokenMetadata contains metadata for token attribution and metering.

limit.description: Maximum tokens allowed in the window. CRD range is typically 1..1e9.

window.description:
Window duration, e.g. "1m", "30s", "2h". Pattern: ^[1-9]\d{0,3}(s|m|h)$,
and at most 8784h (366 days), the longest window MaaS accepts.

v1TokenRateLimit.description: TokenRateLimit caps token usage over a time window.

v1TokenRateLimitStatus.description: TokenRateLimitStatus reports a generated TokenRateLimitPolicy and its model.
